title: Open Coffee pour patterns
description: How water goes onto the coffee in pour-over and AeroPress brewing. Three kinds of record share one list: flow patterns (how the amount of water is spread over time, for example pulse pouring or a ramp-up), kettle movements (where the stream lands, for example a spiral) and recipes (named techniques such as the 4:6 method, written as a timed list of phases). Flow patterns carry an example phase list so every record can be drawn as a pour curve. Part of Roastbook Open Coffee.

$schema.description: Canonical URL of the schema version this file follows.

slug.title: Readable id
slug.description: Lowercase letters and digits in words joined by hyphens, for example ramp-up or hoffmann-better-1-cup. Never renamed or reused.

agitation.title: Agitation
agitation.description: Extra agitation during or after a phase. swirl: turn the whole brewer to move the slurry; gentle_swirl: a light swirl that only flattens the bed; stir: stir the slurry with a spoon or paddle; spin: the Rao spin, a quick swirl after the last pour that flattens the bed for an even drawdown.

path_segment.title: Path segment
path_segment.description: One part of the stream's path seen from above. Positions are fractions of the coffee bed radius: 0 is the centre, 1 the paper wall.

shape.description: point: the stream stays in one place (radius is the distance from the centre); circle: small circles at radius around the centre; spiral: from the centre out to radius and back (turns full turns each way); line: sweeps back and forth across the bed, radius on each side of the centre.

radius.description: Distance from the centre as a fraction of the bed radius (0 to 1).

turns.description: Full turns of a circle or spiral, or sweeps of a line, per pour.

angle_degrees.description: Direction of a line or of an off-centre point, in degrees clockwise from the top.

flow_point.title: Flow point
flow_point.description: One point of a recorded or drawn flow curve. Points are joined by straight lines.

at_seconds.description: Seconds since the start of the phase.

grams_per_second.description: Flow from the kettle at that moment, in grams of water per second.

phase.title: Phase
phase.description: One step of a brew. Phases run one after the other; a recipe's timeline is the sum of their durations.

id.description: Id of the phase, unique within the record, for example bloom or pour-2.

type.description: pour: water goes onto the coffee; hold: wait without pouring (bloom rest, pause between pulses, an immersion steep); drawdown: the last water drains through the bed; press: a plunger pushes the brew through the filter, as in an AeroPress.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the phase in seconds, at the recipe's default amounts.

water_fraction.description: Share of the total brew water poured in this phase (0 to 1). Only on pour phases; the pour phases of a recipe add up to 1.

flow.description: Shape of the flow within a pour phase. constant: the same rate throughout; ramp_up: starts slow and gets faster; ramp_down: starts fast and gets slower; custom: follows flow_curve.

flow_curve.description: Flow over time for a custom pour, for example a recorded reference pour. Required when flow is custom.

movement.description: Id of the kettle movement record used in this pour phase.

note.description: Short instruction in plain words, for example "pour in the centre only".

scored.description: Whether a follow-along app should compare the brewer's pour with this phase. Absent means yes for pour phases and no otherwise.

name.description: Common name, for example Pulse pouring or 4:6 Method.

kind.description: flow: a way of spreading the water over time; movement: where the kettle stream lands; recipe: a named technique that combines flow patterns and movements.

description.description: Short neutral explanation in our own words.

creator.description: Person or company that published the recipe, as they publish it, for example James Hoffmann or April Coffee Roasters. Recipes only.

published_year.description: Year the recipe was first published.

url.description: Where the creator published the recipe (their own page or video).

brew_methods.description: Ids of brew methods from the brew-methods dataset this record applies to, for example v60.

flow_patterns.description: Ids of the flow pattern records a recipe combines, for example bloom and pulse.

defaults.title: Reference brew
defaults.description: The ratio the recipe is built on and the example brew the phases are written for. Water amounts scale with the dose as scaling says; dose_g and brew_water_g are the creator's published example and match brew_ratio within 1%.

brew_ratio.description: Grams of brew water per gram of coffee, for example 16.7 for 1:16.7. The main fact of the recipe: any dose works at this ratio.

dose_g.description: Ground coffee in the published example brew, in grams.

brew_water_g.description: Total brew water in the published example brew, in grams.

bypass_water_g.description: Water added to the finished brew, or put in the cup before it, in the published example brew, in grams. Not part of brew_water_g or brew_ratio; it scales with the dose like the brew water. Mostly used by AeroPress recipes that brew a concentrate.

scaling.title: Scaling
scaling.description: How the recipe changes when the amounts change.

water.description: proportional: every pour keeps its share of the water; fixed: pours keep their gram amounts.

timing.description: proportional: phase durations grow with the water; fixed: phase durations stay the same for other doses (the usual case: creators keep their timings and adjust the grind).

phases.description: The timed steps in order. On a flow pattern, an example that shows the pattern.

path.description: The stream's path seen from above, for kettle movements. Several segments mean the movement switches between them.

roast.title: Roast level
roast.description: Roast level a temperature applies to, from light (filter roasts, often called Nordic or ultra-light at the far end) to dark.

temperature.title: Brew temperature
temperature.description: Brew water temperature as the creator gives it: one range for every coffee, ranges by roast level, or just off the boil when no number is given. A missing value means the creator does not say.

celsius.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius for any roast, as a range (min, max) or one value (typical).

by_roast.description: Temperatures that depend on the roast level, lightest first.

off_the_boil.description: true when the creator says to use water just off the boil ("boiling", "as hot as possible") without a number. At sea level that is close to 100 °C.

note.description: Short extra advice in plain words, for example "for dark roasts wait 15 to 25 seconds after the boil".

roast_temperature.title: Temperature by roast
roast_temperature.description: A temperature range for one or more roast levels.

roasts.description: Roast levels this range applies to.

celsius.description: Temperature in degrees Celsius for these roasts.
